assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_SAKURA_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (19,500 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of the DA Lycoris Otome Sakura, Fuki's partner after Takina, in the Japanese TV series and the Friends Shorts. It locates her by episode, cue, timecode, retained frame and the project's claim and visual IDs; its television scenes are E03, E07, E09 and E11-E13, with Shorts 05 and 06, and it reads the Short 05 restraint device through the owner's 23 November listening return. The section 'What a partner can still say' (Asaura's Recovery days and Gluttony days, the Reload 02 contributor story and Recollect V02) is an attributed print comparison outside the television continuity, and no prediction here rests on it, including the cold-condition training report it gives her. The checkpoint, readings and reconciliation records it links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them directly. The discovery row does not claim speech or ethics. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Her history belongs to her at every state, so far as the portrait gives it, which is little: in the television evidence her age, upbringing and history before DA are undisclosed. Located present states: newly appointed as Fuki's partner, announcing that Takina has no seat, teasing Chisato from under Fuki's supervision, losing the mock battle, apologizing to Fuki for her shooting and accepting Fuki's correction (E03); assuming the cover story, ordering the matcha dango special and protesting when Fuki calls her out (E07); asking for a quick parfait, saying 'good for you' to Takina and complaining outside that Takina should be happier (E09); hurrying the team, 'again?' at Takina's departure, blaming Erika, asking how to report it, and calling the operation a competition (E11); saying she does not want to disobey because she wants credit and to become a First, going with Fuki to the control room, relief that the affair will be hidden because it affects her prospects, and telling Erika to give Takina proper thanks (E12); wounded, then back at the café in a dark uniform ordering the special, with no promotion shown (E13). Shorts 05 and 06 are placed as the portrait places them, without a calendar. Nothing after E13; print stories are outside scope.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait gives a located account of a junior who wants the place, the credit and the red uniform of a First: announcing Takina's lost seat while presenting herself as the respectable answer (E03), arguing that the operation is a competition and protesting another team's credit (E11), stating that she wants credit and to become a First and welcoming the cover-up because it affects her prospects (E12), and asking to wear a First's uniform (Short 05). Its closing section makes narrow predictions: impatience when a place is discussed before anyone has shown what they can do, a competitive response before a gracious one when she proves wrong, acceptance of concrete correction from Fuki (E03), blunt credit to a colleague (E12), and loud protest followed by compliance when a departure is ordered. It predicts her mistakes: overconfidence in her accuracy and pressing after advice to stop (E03), misreading how much has changed for Takina (E09), and blaming Erika beyond what she knows (E11). Not B: the portrait says her E12 answer 'cannot supply a tractable doctrine of when orders deserve obedience'; it shows only that she goes when Fuki personally takes her along. What she would choose if the First uniform ceased to matter, and her view of institutional secrecy under personal harm, remain open, and nobody has asked her to give up a seat. Ambition, avoiding disobedience and staying with Fuki would diverge in a new choice that Fuki does not direct, so this is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. The portrait also leaves open whether the E03 correction taught her anything. Not D: the ambition pattern and her compliance under protest are each located across several episodes.

Located states: new partner and defeated challenger (E03); a junior who follows her senior and loses her dessert (E07, E09); a teammate who objects to Takina's second departure and blames Erika (E11); an objector who goes with Fuki, then welcomes the cover-up and tells Erika to give proper thanks (E12); wounded, then back at the café without promotion (E13). The portrait contrasts her E03 taunt with her E09 congratulation, and her E11 blame of Erika with her E12 instruction to Erika, but explains each by a new audience and situation rather than a change in her. Not B: no inner transition is located, and whether she learned from E03 is left open. Not D: the states are located by episode and cue.

Located register shifts, given in English: demanding a stranger's identity, then abruptly addressing a senior and commander once Fuki names Chisato, then teasing 'the hero' from under Fuki's supervision (E03); a bored answer to Fuki's command (E03); a curt assumption that the news has a cover story (E07); accusing Fuki of putting on airs in front of Mika (E07); 'good for you' to Takina (E09); 'again?' (E11); addressing Chisato as 'the tower' (Short 05). The discovery row does not claim speech, and the portrait quotes no Japanese form of hers: no self-reference, address term or sentence ending. Not C: the shifts are described in English without forms that constrain her Japanese. Not E: changes of address with a stranger, seniors and peers are located with cues.

Located and repeated: ordering the matcha dango special and losing it when Fuki calls her out on duty (E07), asking for whichever parfait comes quickest (E09), ordering the special at last and saying she can finally eat it (E13), and wanting parfait while sick in bed (Short 06); asking to wear Chisato's red uniform, and admitting she once tried on Fuki's in secret (Short 05). The closing section predicts that she asks for another minute over a postponed dessert, stays if allowed, and protests loudly and goes if ordered. Not B: there is no routine or life beyond the café and the dorm visit. Not D: a repeated, located habit with a predictable response to interruption.

Directed differences: Fuki (apology and accepted correction after the match, compliance with protest, the accusation of putting on airs before Mika, going with her to the control room, and a secret try-on of her uniform; E03, E07, E12, Short 05); Takina (the lost-seat taunt, 'good for you', 'again?', telling Erika to thank her, and the witness Takina silences in Short 05; E03, E09, E11, E12); Erika (blamed for the vacancy in E11, told to give proper thanks in E12); Chisato (an unknown, then the famous senior she teases, then 'the tower' who lends the uniform; E03, Short 05); Hibana (the disagreement over whether it is a competition, E11). Not A: the portrait gives no access to what she wants from Fuki beyond the partnership, and says her E09 greeting is neither disingenuous nor proof of friendship. Not C: each relationship has located acts and a stated difference.

Located avowals: wanting credit and to become a First, and relief at the cover-up because it affects her prospects (E12); wanting the special and the parfait (E07, E09, E13, Short 06); calling the view in Chisato's uniform the view from First (Short 05). The portrait says nothing in E12 gives a doctrine of obedience, leaves her sensory access and thoughts when wounded open (E13), and grounds its café expectations in her stated appetite and practical compliance 'rather than any unshown interior'. Not B: no motive is stated for going with Fuki over her own objection. Not D: her central ambition is avowed in her own words and located.

Located modes with outcomes: provoking Takina and pressing the mock battle after advice to stop, ending in defeat and an apology to Fuki (E03); protesting beyond the café when called out, and going (E07); 'again?' and blame on Erika, followed by the practical question of how to report the departure (E11); arguing with Hibana that it is a competition (E11); stating her objection to disobeying and then going with Fuki (E12). The portrait conditions the modes on authority: a peer gets blame or argument, a senior's decision gets protest and compliance. Not A: the only located case of an objection on a substantive matter is E12, where Fuki decides for her, and conflict with a commander or a stranger is not sampled. Not C: the modes are varied, located and conditioned on who holds the decision.

Located positions only, without deliberation: assuming that a news cover story is accepted practice, before a former DA employee who objects (E07); not wanting to disobey because she wants credit (E12); welcoming the cover-up of the affair because it affects her prospects (E12). The portrait says the E07 exchange gives no evidence of how she would defend the cover story to a survivor, and that her independent view of institutional secrecy under personal harm remains open; the row does not claim ethics. Not C: she is never shown weighing a choice. Not E: the positions are stated in her own words and located.

Located sardonic play: calling the story about Takina that of a movie murderer, the kind she likes, while presenting herself as the answer to it (E03); teasing Chisato from under Fuki's supervision and remarking how well the bickering seniors get along (E03); the joke about why Fuki's uniform did not fit and calling Chisato's the view from First (Short 05); laughing at Takina in red (Short 05). Not B: the portrait gives no account of when the teasing stops or how a target's answer changes it. Not D: teasing with distinct targets is located in several scenes.

One dedicated portrait locates each television and shorts scene it uses by cue, timecode, frame and claim ID, and reads the Short 05 restraint device through the owner's listening return. Not B: the row curates only this derived item; about a quarter of the text is print comparison outside the continuity; its author undertook no native synchronized re-audition; and the portrait does not say that it covers every scene in which she appears. Not D: every scene it relies on is located.

Located bounds against overreading: her E03 familiarity with the tower story tells her nothing about how Chisato fights; the E07 exchange gives no evidence of how she would defend a cover story to a survivor, and her accusation gives no access to Fuki's reason; her E09 greeting rests on an overheard reason and an inference, and is neither disingenuous nor proof of friendship; her E12 answer gives no doctrine of obedience; her E12 explanation of why Erika stayed does not prove every command decision; E13 shows no promotion for her, and the uniform remark belongs to Fuki's red; Chisato's permission carries no authority over Fuki's uniform; her Short 05 laugh and muffled answer are not assent to restraint, and the attachment of the restraint is off-shot; and Short 06 gives no diagnosis and no rivalry with Erika. Not A: no forecast about her is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

Television states are placed by episode, cue and timecode. Not B: there is no story calendar, her history before DA is undisclosed, and Shorts 05-06 are not placed in the episode sequence. Not D: the episode states are precisely located.

conditions: Illustrative lines in English rendering only, in the located situations: a pointed reassurance to a displaced rival, teasing a senior from under her own senior's supervision, a curt statement of accepted practice, protest at losing a dessert, 'again?' at a teammate's departure, and blunt instruction to a peer to give thanks (E03, E07, E09, E11, E12).
Excluded: any Japanese self-reference, address term or sentence ending, extended or private speech, and her speech to a commander.
scenario_readiness.note: The discovery row does not claim speech. The located situations constrain what she says, in English rendering; nothing in the evidence constrains her Japanese.

conditions: A place, rank or partnership is discussed before anyone has shown what they can do: predict impatience, a claim on the place and a pointed remark at a rival's expense (E03, E11; the closing section).
Concrete correction from Fuki after a loss: predict an apology to Fuki and a startled question testing the correction; whether she has learned from it is excluded (E03).
A teammate leaves work in a way that may cost the team a result: predict objection, blame on the person, and a practical question about how to report it (E11).
Fuki personally takes her along on an unauthorized course: predict a stated objection about credit and disobedience, then going with Fuki (E12).
A treat interrupted by a senior's order: predict a request for another minute, loud protest, and compliance (E07, E09; the closing section).
When she proves wrong, predict a competitive response before a gracious one; when a colleague is owed credit, predict that she says so bluntly (E03, E12; the closing section).
Include her mistakes: overconfidence in her accuracy, pressing after advice to stop, misreading what has changed for someone else, and blame beyond what she knows (E03, E09, E11).

Exclude: giving up a seat, a choice between obedience and ambition that Fuki does not direct, defending a victim in a formal review, repair volunteered to a stranger, her choices if the First rank ceased to matter, and institutional secrecy under personal harm.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Television E03-E13, from her appointment as Fuki's partner to her return to the café after E13's wound, with Shorts 05-06 placed without a calendar. Before E12 she has objected to departures but not been asked to break an order herself; at E12 she goes with Fuki; at E13 she is wounded and is not promoted. Nothing after E13.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Fuki as senior and partner, Takina as the girl whose seat she took, Erika and Hibana as teammates, Chisato as a famous senior, and Mika as café owner. A comparable new senior, rival or teammate is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: DA training, headquarters and field operations, and the café, in the series' Tokyo.
No print scene, no home life or history before DA, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation follows the portrait's closing section. The motive that decides between ambition, avoiding disobedience and staying with Fuki is not established, so a choice Fuki does not direct is excluded.

conditions: Café visits with Fuki and the group: ordering a dessert, asking for a quick one when time is short, protesting when called away and going, and asking to try on a First's uniform when it may be lent (E07, E09, E13, Shorts 05-06).
Excluded: home life, leisure on her own, and any social setting the television evidence does not sample.
scenario_readiness.note: Repeated café scenes give her own choices; ordinary life beyond them would be invented.
Her positions on cover stories and credit are stated but never weighed; the portrait leaves her view of institutional secrecy under personal harm open, and the row does not claim ethics.
The portrait gives her no romantic interest or choice; her bond with Fuki is presented as a partnership with a senior.

conditions: Team work under Fuki: training and a mock battle, an information run, an operation framed as a competition for credit, and the control-room assignment (E03, E07, E11, E12).
Predict that she treats recognition and advancement as stakes, asks the practical reporting question, and complies with a senior's assignment under protest.
Excluded: her training history, any command of her own, promotion, and dealings with DA command.
scenario_readiness.note: Her work under Fuki is the best-located part of the portrait.

known_limits.statement: Her E12 answer shows only that she acts despite her stated objection when Fuki personally takes her along; the portrait says it cannot supply a doctrine of when orders deserve obedience.
What she would choose if the First uniform ceased to matter, and her independent view of institutional secrecy under personal harm, remain open; nobody has asked her to give up a seat freely.
The E03 defeat and Fuki's correction can teach her something without settling whether she has learned it.
Accepting concrete correction from Fuki (E03) and giving a colleague blunt credit (E12) do not establish that she would volunteer the same repair to a stranger or defend a victim in a formal review.
Her E09 congratulation rests on an overheard reason and an inference about Takina's day; it is neither disingenuous nor proof that they have become friends.
E13 shows her back at the café in a dark uniform with no promotion; the remark about a uniform belongs to Fuki's red.
Her Short 05 laugh and muffled answer are not assent to restraint; Takina's use of a cable-tie launcher is strongly inferable from earlier television uses, and how the lines attach is off-shot.
The Asaura prose, Reload 02 and Recollect V02 scenes, including the cold-condition training report, are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity and are not used for prediction.
Her age and history before DA are undisclosed in the television evidence.
No Japanese form of her speech is quoted, and the row does not claim speech.
Untested: a choice between obedience and ambition that Fuki does not direct, dealings with a commander, and a stranger's or victim's claim on her.
